newsitem.title: UK: Virgin may seek five UK rail franchises.
newsitem.headline: Virgin may seek five UK rail franchises.

text.p: Entreprenuer Richard Branson's Virgin group could bid for five of the remaining 12 British rail passenger businesses still to be transferred to the private sector, a company spokesman said on Sunday.

The spokesman said the company was committed to bidding for the Cross Country and West Anglia Great Northern franchises while it was "very, very likely" to go for the West Coast Main Line and Thameslink services. It is also looking at the Scotrail franchise in Scotland.
Cross Country runs long-distance services the length and breadth of England while West Anglia Great Northern serves Stansted, the airport just east of London.
The West Coast Main Line service is a key artery between London and Glasgow while the Thameslink operation links London's northern and southern suburbs.
Five rail passenger businesses officially transferred to the private sector on Sunday, meaning more than half of the country's passenger network has been privatised.
Only 12 of Britain's 25 train operating companies remain in state hands and the government hopes to sell off as many as possible ahead of a general election due by May.
